aboutPage.headline: We're building the revenue layer the next decade of physical retail will run on.
aboutPage.subhead: Bidygo was born in Yerevan from one observation: every retailer we knew was losing customers to the same problem — shoppers walking out because the shelf price was a few percent too high. The tools for fixing that problem were stuck in 1995. So we built new ones.

thesis.headline: Physical retail isn't dying. It's just under-instrumented.
thesis.para1: Most of the "death of retail" narrative is wrong. Foot traffic is steady, basket sizes are growing, and physical conversion still dwarfs online for most considered purchases.
thesis.para2: What's broken is the instrumentation. Stores have one price (the shelf), one signal (POS), and no way to talk to shoppers in the moment a decision is being made. That's a software problem, not an industry-decline problem.
thesis.para3: Bidygo fixes the instrumentation. Shoppers can act on what they see, in real-time. Retailers can respond, in real-time. Every interaction becomes data. Every walk-out becomes an opportunity.

principles.headline: A few principles we keep coming back to.

items.title: Retailers stay in control.
items.body: We never lower a price the retailer didn't authorize. Bidygo is a software layer, not a marketplace.

items.title: Shoppers stay informed.
items.body: Counter offers, accept rates, average response time — every shopper sees the same data the retailer does.

items.title: Software beats spreadsheets.
items.body: Every pricing decision should be auditable, repeatable, and tunable. No more 'the manager said okay.'

items.title: Data outlasts deals.
items.body: Even a declined offer is useful. We treat the rejection curve as carefully as the acceptance curve.

items.title: Trust compounds.
items.body: Both sides learn from every interaction. The platform gets smarter the longer you use it.

items.title: Local first, then global.
items.body: We build for Armenian shop owners because we know them. The patterns generalize wherever shops sell to shoppers.

objections.q: We don't want customers controlling our prices.
objections.a: They don't. Your dashboard rules govern every response automatically, and your shelf price never moves. Bidygo is a private negotiation channel — not a customer-facing discount.

objections.q: We already run sales and promotions.
objections.a: Promotions discount everyone, including the shoppers who'd have paid full price. Bidygo only converts the ones who were about to leave — the rest still pay your shelf price.

objections.q: Our margins can't take more pressure.
objections.a: That's exactly the point. Floors, ceilings, and counter rules are yours — set once in the dashboard. Bidygo accepts only what fits your rules. Edge cases stay visible so you can adjust the rule, not the offer.

objections.a: Two weeks in one store and one category. We don't replace your POS, we work alongside it. Staff training takes 90 minutes.

whyBidygoPage.headline: Why shoppers walk out — and how Bidygo brings them back.
whyBidygoPage.subhead: Physical shops have always had one shelf price for everyone — so every day they either lose the sale or lose the margin. Bidygo is the controlled middle that ends that trade-off: you win back the sales you're losing, keep your price, and finally see the demand you were missing.
whyBidygoPage.momentTitle: The last two minutes before someone leaves.
whyBidygoPage.momentBody1: Step into almost any high-street shop on a busy afternoon. The shopper finds the product. They like it. They pause at the price.
whyBidygoPage.momentBody2: They pull out their phone. They check three other shops. Sometimes they ask the staff for a better price. Most of the time, they just put the box down and walk out the door.
whyBidygoPage.momentBody3: Your shelf didn't change. Your stock didn't move. You don't know what they would have paid. You don't know which shop they walked to next. The data is gone the moment they cross the threshold.
whyBidygoPage.truthTitle: Three truths about how shoppers actually behave.

truthPoints.title: Shoppers don't all value the same price the same way.
truthPoints.body: The same shoe at the same shelf price will close one shopper and lose another. Your shelf price is a compromise — not a match.

truthPoints.title: Asking out loud is awkward.
truthPoints.body: Most shoppers won't haggle in front of staff. They'll smile, say they'll think about it, and leave. You never learn what number would have worked.

truthPoints.title: Coupons train people to wait.
truthPoints.body: Public discounts give margin to people who would have paid full price — and teach everyone else to come back during the next sale. You lose twice.
